description: The beta-decay rate carries the single-crossing Skein amplitude squared exactly ONCE (prf:trace-ratio-observable: |M_q|^2 = |skein_amp|^2 * |tr(par)/tr(dau)|^2). The merged substitutionRateFactor squares sSq, which is already s^2, so it computes |W|^2/s^4 = 11875.44 where the rate gets |W|^2/s^2 = 129.405107404 -- every '10^4' in the qou-ix74/pfh7/q2l7 arc is high by 1/s^2 = 91.77x. The verdict of qou-ix74 survives (129x still cannot explain a 10-17 % overshoot); its magnitude does not. Separately, qou-q2l7's 'order derived' claim is RETRACTED: |W|^2/s^k diverges as q->1 because W(1) = 1/4 != 0, so the -96 leading value of (J-1)/s^2 -- a ratio whose numerator DOES vanish -- was never its leading constant. Every exact identity of qou-q2l7 is untouched. Third, prf:hadron-half-life multiplies |W|^2 by a |M_q|^2 that still contains s^2, so the live formula carries the vertex trace AND its own single-crossing approximation; which of the three readings is intended is an author decision, recorded and not picked.

convention.anchor: proton pin (Q_50_DIGIT_STR); identities exact in q

substitution_factor.verdict: the qou-ix74 negative SURVIVES -- 129x cannot explain a measured 10-17 % overshoot -- but '10^4' and 'four orders of magnitude' are withdrawn in favour of '~129x, two orders'

retracted_order_claim.claim: qou-q2l7: the ORDER of the substitution factor is derived, 96^2 = 9216 against 11875
retracted_order_claim.why_it_fails: |W|^2/s^k diverges as q->1 for k >= 1 (W(1) = 1/4 != 0, s^2(1) = 0), so it has no leading constant; -96 is the leading value of (J-1)/s^2, whose numerator vanishes because V_K(1) = 1 for every knot
retracted_order_claim.what_survives: every exact identity: W*[2]_q^2 = q^20*V(q^-2); J - 1 = -h_4*h_6/q^10; (J-1)/s^2 = -G_8*G_12/q^19; couplingRatio(1) = -96

readings.A_double_count: item 3's s^2 IS the vertex coupling => rate too small by s^2 ~ 0.0109, half-life too long by ~92x
readings.B_replaces_is_wrong: nothing was replaced, a factor was added; item 3 must say what its s^2 is
readings.C_item_3_stale: the tables use s^2 alone and match neither the pre- nor the post-W formula

vertex_double_count.source_leans_toward: A -- prf:trace-ratio-observable calls its skein_amp 'the Skein amplitude at the beta-decay vertex'
vertex_double_count.decision: AUTHOR'S -- not picked here; no number above depends on it

affected_artifacts: QOU.Braiding.WeakVertexT35.substitutionRateFactor (and its two ten-thousand envelope theorems) -- merged PR #6715

assertions.name: sSq_is_already_s_squared
assertions.note: sSq q = (q-1)^2/q IS (q^(1/2) - q^(-1/2))^2 identically, so squaring it gives s^4 -- the name reads as 's, squared' and was consumed as though it were 's'

assertions.name: nothing_else_in_the_rate_carries_an_s
assertions.note: [2]_q is full-scale; the pair Skein denominator is the half-scale SUM q^(1/2)+q^(-1/2), not s; Q ~ h_1 = q - q^-1 is full-scale. So s enters the rate once, squared, via |M_q|^2

assertions.name: merged_substitution_factor_uses_s_to_the_fourth
assertions.note: (weakVertexTrace q)^2/(sSq q)^2 = |W|^2/s^4 = 11875.4418937 -- the figure merged in PR #6715 and repeated in #6735, #6765

assertions.name: corrected_substitution_factor_is_one_hundred_twenty_nine
assertions.note: |W|^2/s^2 = 129.405107404 is the factor the rate actually gets

assertions.name: error_factor_is_one_over_s_squared
assertions.note: the two differ by exactly 1/s^2 = 91.7694991484, so every '10^4' figure in the arc is high by ~92x

assertions.name: substitution_factor_has_no_finite_classical_limit
assertions.note: W(1) = 1/4 != 0 while s^2(1) = 0, so |W|^2/s^k diverges for k >= 1: there is NO leading constant, at either power

assertions.name: the_minus_ninety_six_belongs_to_a_different_ratio
assertions.note: (J-1)/s^2 -> -96 because J(1) = 1 makes the NUMERATOR vanish (V_K(1) = 1 for every knot); W(1) = 1/4 does not vanish. So -96 cannot be the leading constant of |W|^2/s^k -- qou-q2l7's 'order derived' bridge is RETRACTED, not re-scoped

assertions.name: qou_q2l7_identities_are_untouched
assertions.note: the Jones-Markov relation, J - 1 = -(q^8-1)(q^12-1)/q^20, and the cyclotomic ratio all still hold: the mathematics of qou-q2l7 survives, only its bridge to the rate does not

assertions.name: negative_of_qou_ix74_survives_at_the_corrected_magnitude
assertions.note: 129x is still far too large to explain a measured 10-17 % overshoot, so substituting |W|^2 for s^2 remains a scope-(a) negative -- the verdict stands, the magnitude was wrong by 92x
